sessions.intent: Start a fresh C#-developer doc tree mirroring PLang/app/ — fundamentals first (the app root and the module system), always mapping plang -> C# -> source.

before.assumptions: Existing Documentation/architecture.md is stale (old App.System/.Service/.User, .Goals, Data with Type? Type). app-tree.md is closer but predates the lowercase-nodes rename. The website docs/ is for PLang users, not C# devs. Runtime2 is now a deep OBP tree: PLang/app/**/this.cs, path mirrors namespace, @this is each folder's primary class aliased in GlobalUsings.
before.risk: Docs stating stale truth is worse than no docs. Must verify every assertion against current source. Scope risk: the type/item lattice is huge; v1 must stay on the fundamentals Ingi named (app, module) plus the reading conventions, not boil the ocean.

actions.context: Foundational 'how to read this codebase' page + the app root. Initially drafted at Documentation/app/start.md; moved into the code tree at Ingi's direction ('why not put them in plang/app/'). Grounded in PLang/app/this.cs, GlobalUsings.cs, type/item/this.cs; verified against source, not copied from the stale architecture.md.

The module system: registry, discovery (Discover + [Action], module name = namespace segment after app.module), the action handler pattern, attribute reference, dispatch via the real decide.pr, and 'type is the role'. Points to os/system/modules/<module>/ for the runtime teaching prose rather than duplicating it (Ingi's choice).

The file module worked example — all seven actions mapped to source. Read read.cs, save.cs, exists.cs, copy.cs and grepped move/delete/list for accurate signatures, returns, and cacheable flags; verified [Default(false)] on Overwrite and Subfolder=include.
Session plan and summary. Structure decided interactively with Ingi: in-tree docs, start.md per folder + named topic files, depth approved, dev docs point-not-duplicate the teaching layer.

after.status: v1 complete — fundamentals (app root + module system + file worked example) authored and verified against source.
after.notes: Fresh code-mirrored developer doc tree started under PLang/app/ as start.md files. No production C# changed. Next versions extend the tree (type/item, goal, data, channel, event, actor) and retire the stale Documentation/architecture.md.

sessions.intent: Extend the in-tree developer doc tree with the type system (type/) and the value lattice (type/item/) — fundamentals part 2.

before.assumptions: type.@this is the type entity {Name, Kind, Strict, Template} and is itself an item; type.list.@this (AppTypes) is the registry reached at app.type via type.root, selection-only, with the CLR<->plang PlangName map. item.@this is the value apex; type.item.list.@this<T> is the native plang list. The stale Documentation/type-system.md predates these shapes.
before.risk: The type/item subtree is very large (50+ value types, deep number/kind matrix). v2 must cover the fundamentals (entity, registry, apex, item.list, core scalars) and name-but-not-expand the leaves, or it never ships.

actions.context: The type system page. Drafted by a Haiku subagent from a verified-facts brief (I read type/this.cs + type/list/this.cs myself; an Explore agent surveyed root/kind/property/current/convert/format). I verified cited filenames (this.Owns.cs, kind class decl, choice/set/this.cs) against source before commit. Keeps entity vs registry distinct; covers PlangName CLR<->plang map, kind-is-behaviour, format-in-play, current<T,L>, birth vs make.

The value-lattice page. Drafted by a Haiku subagent from a verified-facts brief (Explore agent surveyed item.@this + list/dict + the scalar types). The subagent corrected my brief's rank facts against source; I then verified all 18 Rank => overrides match exactly (null 1000 .. text 100, apex/path 0) and that this.Equality.cs/this.Ladder.cs/this.Generic.cs exist. Full 'how item.list works' section, item.Create rungs, scalar types, number.kind.int, rank/coercion.
v2 bookkeeping. Workflow experiment this version: the two pages were written by Haiku subagents (Ingi's suggestion) and I reviewed/verified every precise claim before committing.

after.status: v2 complete — type system + value lattice pages authored (by Haiku subagents), every precise claim verified against source.
after.notes: Fundamentals now cover app, module, type and the value lattice. One minor stale-source-doc finding recorded (type.list this[System.Type] XML comment says null-on-miss; code returns the clr entity). No production C# changed. Next: goal/data/channel/event/actor pages, then retire stale Documentation/architecture.md + type-system.md.

sessions.intent: "do everything": write start.md for the remaining core concepts — goal, data, channel, event, actor, call, error (Wave A).

before.assumptions: The in-tree start.md pattern is established (v1/v2). Haiku subagents pointed at spine source files + a style brief + the v1/v2 examples produce accurate pages; I verify risky claims. data/channel/event/call are locked-core surfaces — document as-is, propose nothing.
before.risk: Seven pages at once; locked-core accuracy matters most (event list, Data shape, error subclasses). A Haiku writer reading a deep subtree shallowly could assert a wrong signature — mitigated by spine-file targeting + my per-page verification pass before commit.

actions.context: Seven core-concept pages drafted by parallel Haiku subagents, each pointed at its spine source files + the shared style brief + the v1/v2 pages. Writers verified against source and corrected the briefs where wrong (event: real 11-event list, own/declared are classes not events, clause handler is the module action not IClause; error: real subclass keys/statuses; data: Data.Merge does not exist). I quality-read data + call (locked core) in full, spot-verified claims, and reconciled all cross-links.

Review pass: reconciled tree-from-here cross-links (siblings written in parallel were marked 'not yet written'; now linked), and tightened the data page's view-tag passage after verifying Properties carries [Out,Store] AND [JsonIgnore]/[LlmIgnore] (not a contradiction).

after.status: v3 complete — 7 core-concept pages (goal, data, channel, event, actor, call, error) authored by Haiku subagents and verified. Cross-links reconciled.
after.notes: The in-tree developer tree now covers app, module(+file), type(+item), goal, data, channel, event, actor, call, error. Several stale source comments surfaced during verification (recorded as findings, flagged for coder; no production C# edited this pass). Wave B (smaller concepts: setting/store/snapshot/task/test/keepalive/service/warning/parent/shortcut/variable) is scoped and inventoried for the next version.
